captions.detailed: This 3D model is a compact, robust converter designed to turn a standard metal nail into a functional tent peg. It features a central cylindrical housing with a vertical hole for inserting a nail, flanked by two functional wings on a flat baseplate. On one side, there is a rounded extension containing a large hole for securing guy lines, and on the opposite side, a raised vertical peg with a small T-shaped crossbar base to prevent ropes from slipping off. All top and bottom edges are heavily beveled to ensure smooth handling and prevent stress concentration.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric nail-to-tentpeg converter in OpenSCAD. The design should feature a central cylindrical sleeve to house a nail, a flat connection plate extending to one side with a guy line attachment hole, and an extension to the other side supporting a vertical peg with T-shaped horizontal wings to catch ropes. Ensure all external parts have adjustable bevels for smooth edges, and include parameters for nail diameter, clearance, peg height, and hole shift.
captions.factory: The design is built using a custom module, 'bcylinder', which creates a cylinder with beveled top and bottom edges using three stacked cylinders (two tapered for the bevels, one straight for the middle). The main assembly uses a union of these beveled cylinders combined with the 'hull()' operator to create smooth connecting plates from the central nail cylinder to the side hole and the peg. A T-shaped anchor is formed on the peg side using a hull between two offset lateral cylinders. Finally, the 'difference()' operator is used to subtract a straight cylinder for the central nail hole and another for the guy line hole.
